learning_outcomes.text: Students know the importance of assembly and handling technology in production and can explain it.
Students can analyze existing assembly systems and formulate suggestions for improvement.
Students can plan preliminary concepts for assembly and evaluate them.
Students know the fundamentals of assembly planning methodologies, workplace design, and handling technology.
They can abstractly model necessary handling functions.
Students know the particular problems with highly variant assemblies and can name them and know essential approaches to deal with them.
Students can evaluate assembly concepts economically and in terms of their utility.
Students can explain the relationship between an MBOM bill of material structure and the assembly layout and derive essential approaches for controlling assembly from it.
Furthermore, students know essential concepts of digitalization in the specific context of assembly and can evaluate them.
Students can select suitable robots, associated programming methods, and gripping technology for the design of value streams in production.
For this, they are familiar with both the structure of industrial robots and their periphery.
Furthermore, they have an understanding of the powertrain and its control.
In addition, they know mobile robots used in the factory environment for logistics tasks.
They know methods for path planning used for robot control.

syllabus_topics: Importance of assembly and handling technology for production
Organizational forms in assembly
Discussion of different planning cases
Presentation of essential influencing factors for the design of assembly systems
Introduction to exemplary solutions for technical assembly systems
Influences of product design and structure on the design of assembly systems
Procedure for designing assembly systems: process planning, precedence graph, and performance balancing
Determination of assembly structure and degree of automation
Creation of the rough layout of an assembly system
Special features of assembly design for highly variant products
Manual, hybrid, and automated assembly systems, workplace design & ergonomics
Assembly-related supply planning
Assembly control
Handling and its sub-functions: handling devices, transfer systems, and manipulators
Economic aspects of assembly systems
Influences and benefits of digitalization and Industry 4.0 on assembly
Individual components of a robot system: Kinematics, powertrain (incl. control), measurement technology, gripping technology, periphery
Different robot types and handling techniques
Methods for programming robots / control technology and path planning
Mobile robot applications: how motion tasks can be executed through navigation and path planning
